matrix.text: Land use and all modes of transport are integrated, and the adverse effects of traffic generation on the network are managed.
An integrated transport network including public transport, walking, cycling, private vehicles and freight is provided for.
Pedestrian safety and amenity along public footpaths is prioritised.
Road/rail crossings operate safely with neighbouring land use and development.

Development generating trips with potentially more than minor effects, outside the City Centre, Metropolitan Centre, Town Centre and THAB zones and the Centre Fringe Office Control, manages its effects and integrates with the network (travel planning, alternatives to car trips, staging, local improvements).

matrix.text: Major proposals for discretionary consent prepare an integrated transport assessment covering pedestrians, cyclists, public transport users, freight and motorists.

paragraph.text: The depth of this transport assessment is set in proportion to the scale and significance of the proposal's transport effects, as RMA s88(2AA)–(2AB) and Schedule 4 clause 2(3)(c) require. The proposal generates about 612 veh/h (PM) of net vehicle trips. The largest change on any modelled link is +749.5% on Side 2N (AM). Crash flags: crash data not loaded. State highway involvement: none found. Precinct: none. ITA Full likely regardless of GFA: the proposal has a drive-through component. G00907 Table 2: Moderate (Full, consistent with zoning, urban). On that basis an ITA with a network model is proposed. [Author to confirm and record agreement at scoping.]

ok.item: Record the pathway, the lodgement date (planned or actual) and the statutory version the assessment is written against (pre-assent RMA, transition RMA, FTAA as when made)

ok.source: MBCM vol 1 v1.7.5 s1.3, s1.9, s7.2, ch 5; GC 25/01; Minimum information for improvements s9.6
ok.how: P95 cost is entered
ok.refNote: GC 25/01: 2% for years 1–30, 1.5% for years 31–100, 1% from year 101 (non-commercial; commercial 8%); it asks for an 8% sensitivity test on every transport economic analysis, reported with the results. Check the MBCM v1.7.5 s1.9 wording.

ok.item: BCR_N and NPV for every shortlisted option, FYRR for the preferred option, BCR_G where there is third-party funding; exclude transfers, GST, residual values and land-value uplift
Incremental BCR analysis for mutually exclusive options, with target from Table 104 and a +1.0 target test
ok.source: MBCM vol 1 v1.7.5 s6.3, Table 104

ok.item: Choose a fixed or variable trip matrix (VTM probable for large road schemes in major centres); rule of half; RR717 screening for new roads at early stages
ok.source: MBCM vol 1 v1.7.5 s2.2-2.5, s2.13, Table 4
ok.how: Spare Construct warns; the justification is the author's

ok.item: Crash analysis from CAS: 5 years normally (10 years ÷ 2 below 1,500 vpd), method A, B or C, CEC 2nd edition v4
ok.source: MBCM vol 1 v1.7.5 s3.1, Tables 6-7; CEC 2nd ed v4 (May 2026)
ok.refNote: GC 26/01: CEC 2nd edition v4 released 29 May 2026 with MBCM v1.7.5; crash procedures moved into MBCM volume 1.

ok.item: Efficiency rating with WEBs excluded at stage 1; BCR rounding; supporting calculations to avoid L*
ok.source: 2024-27 IPM p9, p27; initial draft IPM 2027-30 pp8-11, 32-33; Minimum information for improvements p10
ok.how: dual band display, with the draft labelled

ok.item: Stage 2 quantitative GPS metrics: freight and general traffic travel time or reliability change at network level, minutes to key destinations, houses enabled, DSI reduction per $100m
ok.source: Initial draft IPM 2027-30 Appendix 1 pp24-29
ok.how: modelled metrics; destination significance and housing classes are entered

ok.item: Model documentation: Transport modelling checks worksheet per period; TMDG validation for the purpose category
ok.source: MBCM vol 1 v1.7.5 s4.1, s4.3; TMDG
ok.how: pre-filled worksheet and validation report; peer review is manual

ok.item: Safe System audits at key stages for NLTF improvement and renewal activities, attached to the TIO application
ok.source: NZTA 2024-27 NLTP Safe System Audit Policy (June 2024)
ok.how: Spare Construct exports an audit pack

ok.item: Programme Investment and LCLR eligibility: activities under $50m, BCR above 1, caps per activity class, no splitting
ok.source: NZTA Programme Investment guidance (6 Jul 2026) pp4, 7, 9; LCLR guidance v1 s5.1, 6
ok.how: flags

ok.item: CBDS per road in cl 3.3 structure; not for new roads or school-gate limits; updated if the limit changes after consultation
ok.source: Setting of Speed Limits Rule 2024 cl 3.2, 3.3; NZTA Rule guidance s5

ok.item: Limit within the Schedule 3 range for the Rule class; Schedule 1 minimum length; 110/120 for NZTA only; variable limit reason

ok.item: School variable limits and travel windows near schools
ok.source: Setting of Speed Limits Rule 2024 cl 1.4, 5.1-5.4

ok.source: LGACA s47C, Sch 4

ok.source: LGA ss102A(3), 197AB, 198B, 199, 199AA, Sch 1AA cl 71

ok.item: IFF levy: benefits inside and outside the levy area and contribution to need
ok.source: IFF Act 2020 ss8, 18, 18A

ok.evidence: Assessment scoped to the matters of discretion

ok.item: Assess against the E27.2 objectives and E27.3 policies. Under E27.3(2), major discretionary proposals prepare an ITA covering pedestrians, cyclists, PT users, freight and motorists
ok.how: Spare Construct auto-fills a policy matrix with links to its evidence; the planner writes the evaluation

ok.item: AEE transport content: actual or potential effects, mitigation, affected persons and consultation, monitoring, and alternatives if a significant adverse effect is likely. Put safety under cl 6(1)(b) and 7(1)(a), not cl 7(1)(f)
ok.how: base vs with-development vs mitigated comparison, and a monitoring template; consultation is manual

ok.item: Define the receiving environment: existing network plus committed projects plus granted consents likely to be implemented. Permitted baseline optional
ok.source: RMA s104(1)(a), s104(2); Queenstown Lakes DC v Hawthorn Estate [2006] NZRMA 424 (CA)
ok.how: the register is entered or imported by the planner; scenarios are built automatically

ok.item: Include cumulative enabled or consented development. Include only planned and funded projects in future networks unless sensitivity-tested. Assess construction, interim years and full build-out
ok.source: AT ITA v2 s3.6.1, s4.2, s4.2.1; NZTA ITA Guide G00907 s5.4
ok.how: scenario matrix with funding-status gating
ok.text: Scenario matrix created; funding gating passes.

ok.item: Set the study area to include arterial, rapid or frequent transit and freight routes with demand increase over 5%, and collectors with increase over 10%
ok.source: AT ITA v2 s4.2.1.1
ok.how: extent test using Future Connect classes
ok.text: Run the extent test (5% / 10%) and store the extent.

ok.item: Generate person trips first, then mode share, distribution and timing. Source and date every rate; review pre-2020 and 2020-22 rates; give evidence for any WFH or TDM discount; estimate freight separately; justify periods covering both development and network peaks
ok.source: AT ITA v2 s3.6.1(i)-(vi), Appendix 1
ok.how: Spare Construct computes and warns; rate choice and justification are the author's

ok.item: Multimodal LOS: PT LOS and delay, PT reach within 400 m-1.2 km walk, pedestrian and cycle LOS, freight on Future Connect routes, queue safety. ANOP tool recommended where any mode's LOS is affected
ok.source: AT ITA v2 s4.1, s4.2.1-4.2.3; ANOP Application v1 (July 2025)
ok.how: bus delay, catchments and ANOP speed/reliability bands; active-mode LOS needs a site audit
ok.evidence: Multimodal LOS tables and ANOP inputs

ok.item: Review the latest 5 years of CAS data near the site and for each altered intersection or access, using a Safe System risk approach. Assess safety effects of the extra trips separately
ok.how: CAS extract, DSI and risk metrics; the author writes the narrative
ok.evidence: Crash tables CR1-CR3 and Safe System commentary
ok.text: Load CAS crashes for the study area.

ok.item: Assess sight distance for new or altered accesses, intersections and crossings to Austroads GRD Part 4A at operating speed, allowing for pending speed-limit changes

ok.how: calculation from NSLR or modelled speed; the site survey is manual

ok.item: Parking: supply against the maximums (no minimums), accessible parking including the E27.6.3.2A(4) activity and zone list, and induced peak trips where a maximum is exceeded

Vehicle access restrictions: within 10 m of an intersection, mapped VAR controls, arterial frontage, within 30 m of a level crossing; City Centre and Key Retail Frontage new crossings non-complying unless excepted

ok.evidence: Access compliance table and E27.8.2(11) evidence

ok.item: Name the correct reviewer and approver: Auckland Council as road controlling authority; the local board for local and collector roads; the transport CCO (AT) for PT; NZTA for state highways; KiwiRail for rail. Name the requiring authority correctly after the transfer date

ok.how: a per-link authority resolver; the planner confirms whether a cl 8(2) direction has ended the transitional period
ok.evidence: Authority table and an affected-operator list
ok.text: Authority table ready; confirm whether a cl 8(2) direction ended the transitional period.

ok.item: State why the depth of transport assessment is proportionate to the scale and significance of effects
ok.source: RMA s88(2AA)-(2AB) (from 20 Oct 2025), Sch 4 cl 1(2), 2(3)(c); s18B (from 30 Oct 2026); FTAA s44

ok.item: A suitably qualified, named author adopts the assessment and complies with the expert Code of Conduct
ok.source: AUP E27.9(4); Environment Court Practice Note 2023 s9.3
ok.how: Spare Construct provides the sign-off block and disclosure appendix
ok.evidence: Qualifications, sign-off, Code of Conduct statement
ok.text: Not signed off: exports carry the DRAFT watermark.

ok.item: Identify the data, facts, assumptions and literature relied on, with dates and sources; supply all model input data

ok.how: provenance register and full input export
ok.evidence: Assumptions register, data vintage table, input data pack
ok.text: Trip rates without a source or year: Houses, Retail, Supermarket, Office, Apartments

ok.item: Run sensitivity and uncertainty analyses on trip generation, mode share, assignment and background growth. Run a funded-only network if none are run, and a no-PT-uplift case where PT improvements are assumed
ok.source: Practice Note 2023 s9.3(a)(x); AT ITA v2 s3.6.1(v), Appendix 1; RMA s32(2)(c)
ok.how: sensitivity battery with tipping points
ok.text: No sensitivity scenario yet.

ok.item: Report model calibration and validation against the agreed TMDG purpose category (A-G). Do not present meeting the criteria as proof that the model is fit for purpose
ok.source: NZTA Transport Model Development Guidelines (1 Sept 2019) s5.3-5.8, Tables 1-5
ok.how: GEH bands, R² and slope, %RMSE, journey times against the category; the author justifies the category
ok.evidence: Validation appendix and a model-status badge on every output

ok.item: Identify zone, controls and precinct under operative and PC120-proposed maps before testing E27.6.1

ok.how: AUP GIS lookup, with a dual-layer warning where PC120 proposes a change

ok.item: Test Table E27.6.1.1 thresholds, apply the exemptions, and report tier 1 (TA1, T1A, T2A, T3A only) or tier 2

ok.refNote: AUP modification schedule 2026: PC79 fully operative 8 May 2026; no later E27 change listed.

ok.how: Spare Construct auto-fills a policy matrix with links to its evidence; the planner writes the evaluation

ok.item: AEE transport content: actual or potential effects, mitigation, affected persons and consultation, monitoring, and alternatives if a significant adverse effect is likely. Put safety under cl 6(1)(b) and 7(1)(a), not cl 7(1)(f)
ok.how: base vs with-development vs mitigated comparison, and a monitoring template; consultation is manual

ok.item: Define the receiving environment: existing network plus committed projects plus granted consents likely to be implemented. Permitted baseline optional
ok.source: RMA s104(1)(a), s104(2); Queenstown Lakes DC v Hawthorn Estate [2006] NZRMA 424 (CA)
ok.how: the register is entered or imported by the planner; scenarios are built automatically

ok.how: scenario matrix with funding-status gating

ok.item: Set the study area to include arterial, rapid or frequent transit and freight routes with demand increase over 5%, and collectors with increase over 10%

ok.item: Assess sight distance for new or altered accesses, intersections and crossings to Austroads GRD Part 4A at operating speed, allowing for pending speed-limit changes

ok.evidence: SSA report with designer responses, or a confirmation it is not required

ok.item: Loading spaces by activity and GFA. One small loading space for 10+ dwellings with arterial-only access and no individual pedestrian access

ok.evidence: Access compliance table and E27.8.2(11) evidence

ok.item: Crossing number, separation and width per frontage; passing bays; queues at gates, drive-throughs and dispensers must not reach the road reserve
